assumptions: Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop (OVRServiceLauncher.exe) are deployed on the same Windows host.
The HTML injection vulnerability in Oculus Browser reliably yields arbitrary code execution rather than solely UI spoofing.

evidence_quotes.quote: inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code.
expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation.

missing_conditions: Verification of co-location of Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop on the same host
Verification that code execution is achieved from the source vulnerability, which only notes it may 'potentially execute code'
Verification of process interaction capabilities allowing the browser process to capture handles exposed by OVRServiceLauncher.exe
response.reason: CVE-2019-3562 allows an attacker to inject HTML into the Oculus Browser UI and 'potentially execute code'. CVE-2021-24038 requires 'an unprivileged process' on a host with Oculus Desktop to obtain an exposed privileged handle from OVRServiceLauncher.exe. Bridging these components requires assuming co-location on the same Windows host and actualizing the modal 'potentially execute code' effect into a functioning local process foothold. Because same-host deployment cannot be inferred and execution is only potential, the edge is conditional.
